name: RestoreX
question: Is RestoreX penile traction therapy for 30 to 90 minutes daily safe, and does it improve penile length and curvature in men with Peyronie's disease?

arms.label: RestoreX penile traction therapy for 30 to 90 minutes daily

design.population: 110 men with Peyronie's disease (diagnosed within 10 years) and curvature of 30 degrees or more, enrolled without exclusion for complex curvature, hourglass deformity, prior Peyronie's treatment or surgery, or calcification.
design.description: Single-center, single-blind (investigator) randomized controlled intent-to-treat trial; no therapy versus traction allocated 1:3
design.locator: p599 abstract; p600 Methods; p602 Table 1; p601 Figure 3 (28 control; 27, 28 and 27 in the once-, twice- and three-times-daily traction groups)

verdictNote: Safety, the primary outcome, was met; length and curvature were secondary outcomes.
takeaway: In 110 men with Peyronie's disease, RestoreX penile traction for 30 to 90 minutes daily had only transient, mild adverse events over 3 months and, versus no therapy, increased penile length (1.5 versus 0 cm) and improved composite curvature (−11.7 versus +1.3 degrees).

reports.label: Randomized phase (3 months)
reports.citation: Ziegelmann M, Savage J, Toussi A, et al. Outcomes of a Novel Penile Traction Device in Men with Peyronie's Disease: A Randomized, Single-Blind, Controlled Trial. *J Urol.* 2019;202(3):599-610.

results.measure: Adverse events through 3 months in men treated with traction
results.note: The paper states that the primary outcome of safety was met and gives no numeric threshold. All de novo events were mild and resolved within minutes of finishing the daily session; no patient withdrew or reduced treatment because of adverse events. Adverse events were tabulated for the traction group only (62 men at 3 months).

values.exp: No moderate or severe adverse events

results.measure: Mean (SD) change at 3 months, pubic symphysis to penile tip
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (62 traction and 27 control men)
results.note: Mean percentage change 10.0% versus 0.4%. Prespecified detectable difference was 0.6 cm (SD 1.0) with 20 men per arm. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change at 3 months, pubic symphysis to glanular corona
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (62 traction and 27 control men)
results.note: Mean percentage change 12.1% versus 2.2%. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change at 3 months, composite curvature
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (62 traction and 27 control men)
results.note: Composite is the sum of primary and secondary curvatures; negative values denote improvement; curvature measured on photographs after pharmacologic erection. Mean percentage change −18.3% versus +3.9%. Prespecified detectable difference was 10 degrees (SD 15) with 20 men per arm. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change at 3 months, primary (larger) curvature
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (62 traction and 27 control men)
results.note: Negative values denote improvement. Mean percentage change −17.8% versus −2.9% (P < 0.01). Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Men with at least 20% curvature improvement plus at least 1-point PDQ bother improvement, or a change from no sexual activity to sexual activity
results.note: The table prints 61 (24.6) for traction and 25 (4) for control, read here as percentages of 61 and 25 evaluable men; the text states 25% of traction men responded. Definition follows the phase III collagenase trials.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in IIEF erectile function domain at 3 months, men with baseline erectile dysfunction (domain score 25 or less)
results.note: Subgroup; its denominator is not reported. The improvement remained significant after controlling for change in curvature (P < 0.01). Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in IIEF erectile function domain at 3 months, all men
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 26 control men)
results.note: Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in IIEF intercourse satisfaction domain at 3 months
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 26 control men)
results.note: Orgasmic function changed by −0.2 versus −0.5 (P = 0.50) and the sexual-desire row by +0.3 versus −0.1 (P = 0.21). Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in IIEF overall satisfaction domain at 3 months
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 26 control men)
results.note: Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Men unable to penetrate at baseline (Sexual Encounter Profile question 2) who could at 3 months
results.note: Denominators are the men answering no at baseline: 8 traction and 4 control.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in psychological and physical domain at 3 months
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 23 control men)
results.note: Negative values denote improvement. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in symptom bother domain at 3 months
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 23 control men)
results.note: Negative values denote improvement. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in penile pain domain at 3 months
results.locator: p603, Table 3 (59 traction and 23 control men)
results.note: Negative values denote improvement. Difference derived by subtraction.

results.measure: Men for whom vaginal intercourse was difficult or impossible at baseline (question 12) and no longer was at 3 months
results.note: The table gives percentages without counts.

results.measure: Traction-treated men with improved curvature at 3 months
results.note: Mean improvement 17.2 degrees (28.2%) among responders; 27% had an improvement of 20 degrees or more and 48% of 20% or more. The denominator is not stated in the text.

results.measure: Traction-treated men with increased length at 3 months
results.note: Mean gain 1.6 cm (10.9%) among responders; 29% gained 2 cm or more. The denominator is not stated in the text.

results.measure: Length and curvature among men reclassified by actual use of once, twice or three times daily
results.note: As-treated subset analysis; the trial was not powered for subgroup differences.

results.measure: Mean (SD not given) length gain by total traction minutes over 3 months
results.note: Post hoc, nonsignificant trend: at least 5,000 minutes (56 minutes daily), 6,000 minutes (67 minutes daily) and 7,000 minutes (78 minutes daily).

results.measure: Preference for RestoreX among men who had used another traction device
results.note: 15 respondents: 86.7% much better and 13.3% somewhat better. Other devices named were PeniMaster, Andropenis, Hydromax, Phallosan Forte, Size Genetics and X4 Labs.

results.measure: Men who would choose RestoreX as first treatment if starting Peyronie's therapy anew
results.note: 54 respondents, who could select more than one option; collagenase 23.6%, oral pills 14.8%, vacuum device 5.6%.

results.measure: Overall satisfaction with traction at 3 months
results.note: Neutral 30.2%, somewhat dissatisfied 3.2%, very dissatisfied 0%.

harms.label: Moderate or severe adverse events
harms.note: No patient withdrew, stopped or reduced treatment because of adverse events or intolerance; most events resolved within seconds or minutes.

harms.label: Penile erythema or discoloration
harms.locator: p603 Table 2 (62 men at 3 months, 81 at baseline)
harms.note: All de novo symptoms were mild.

harms.label: Loss or abnormal penile sensation
harms.locator: p603 Table 2 (62 men at 3 months, 81 at baseline)
harms.note: Present at baseline in a similar proportion.

harms.label: New cold glans, swelling, new bump
Other events
harms.note: New minor curvature resolved by the next treatment, mild skin erosion from tape that resolved in 2 days, delayed urine stream not thought related to traction, skin sensitivity to Coban tape, and testicular pain that resolved after device discontinuation.

delivery.label: Recruitment and enrollment
delivery.value: 800 mailed invitations to men diagnosed within 10 years; 110 enrolled from October 2017 through August 2018

delivery.label: Baseline characteristics
delivery.value: Mean age 58.4 years, Peyronie's disease duration 49.7 months and curvature 59.3 degrees

delivery.label: Whole-cohort severity
delivery.value: Multiplanar curvature 60.0%, indentation 40.0%, hourglass deformity 39.9%, prior Peyronie's therapy 67.9% (collagenase 33.6%, traction 20%, surgery 3.6%), 97% in the chronic phase

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: RestoreX for 30 minutes (15 minutes straight and 15 minutes with counter-bending) once, twice or three times daily for 3 months; men kept a daily diary of traction duration and counter-bending (0 to 120 degrees)

delivery.label: Compliance by dose group
delivery.value: 100% once daily, 82% twice daily and 47% three times daily

delivery.label: Randomized (3:1)
delivery.locator: p602 Table 1; p601 Figure 3 (27, 28 and 27 men in the three traction groups)

delivery.label: Withdrew before the 3-month assessment
delivery.locator: p601 Figure 3 (6, 5 and 8 men in the once-, twice- and three-times-daily groups; reasons not given in the text)

delivery.label: Analysis populations
delivery.value: Intent to treat, with no men excluded for noncompliance; 3-month data were available for 90 men (63 traction, 27 control). Subset analyses reclassified dose by actual use (under 45 minutes per day as once, 45 to 75 as twice, over 75 as three times daily)

delivery.label: Randomization and power
delivery.value: Tables created a priori by primary curvature direction and baseline curvature (30 to 60 versus more than 60 degrees). With 20 men per arm, alpha 0.05 and beta 0.8 as printed, a difference of 0.6 cm (SD 1.0) in length and 10 degrees (SD 15) in curvature was detectable; the trial was not powered for IIEF, PDQ or dose-group differences

delivery.label: Length and curvature measurement
delivery.value: Length: mean of two independent providers blinded to group and prior results. Curvature: photographs by professional surgical photographers after intracavernous Trimix (alprostadil 10 mcg/ml, papaverine 30 mg/ml, phentolamine 1 mg/ml) to an erection of 8 or more out of 10, reviewed by one individual blinded to group and prior assessments

delivery.label: Counter-bending analysis
delivery.value: Greater curvature improvement with counter-bending to 60 to 120 degrees than to 30 degrees (P < 0.01); an early analysis of device design

delivery.label: White indicator line analysis
delivery.value: Men who saw the white line (which indicates more than 3 pounds of force when concealed) most of the time had no length gain (mean −0.17 cm) and less curvature improvement (−2.1 versus −13.9 degrees, P = 0.02) than men who kept it concealed; an early analysis of device design

delivery.label: Device technique
delivery.value: Straight stretch to bury the white indicator line and counter-bending to about 90 degrees; non-compliance defined as failing either on most uses or traction on fewer than 90% of recommended days

delivery.label: Funding and disclosure
delivery.value: Internal Mayo Clinic funds and an anonymous patient gift; PathRight Medical donated the devices; the corresponding author reports a financial interest or other relationship with PathRight Medical

Additional gain from months 3 to 6 in men continuing traction from the randomized phase

results.measure: Gain in length to the glanular corona from baseline to 6 months with traction of at least 15 minutes per day during months 3 to 6 (as-treated; range across the original traction and original control groups)
results.note: The authors describe this as the largest gain reported for any traction device.

Men in the original traction arm analyzed as treated (n=37) with length gain at 6 months

results.note: Among responders, mean improvement was 16.8 degrees (35.8%) in primary and 21.4 degrees (32.8%) in composite curvature.

results.measure: Change at 6 months to glanular corona, original control versus original traction group, as-treated (men using the device at least 15 minutes per day during months 3 to 6)
results.locator: p2467 Table 2 (37 original traction and 14 original control men); difference derived by subtraction
results.note: SD 1.1 cm (original traction) and 2.0 cm (original control). Controls used the device on an open-label basis from month 3, so this is not a controlled comparison.

results.measure: Change at 6 months, original control versus original traction group
results.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov results, outcome measure 'Change in Penile Curvature' (14 original control and 37 original traction men); difference derived by subtraction
results.note: Negative values denote improvement. Registry SD 18.1 degrees (original traction) and 18.6 degrees (original control). Controls used the device on an open-label basis from month 3, so this is not a controlled comparison.
